coupling.rationale: Components depend on typed per-page view models, data access is centralized, and server/client code has a clear seam; only minor leaks (raw API models in templates, one service injection in a presentational component).

evidence: app/src/app/pokedex-data.ts:19-24 — CardEntry captures the real variation (species vs ref, optional types, optional note)
app/src/app/pokedex-data.ts:125-149 — cardsFor unifies ref→species mapping, alt-form exclusion, dedup, dex ordering for three pages
app/src/app/pokemon-cards.ts:14-50 — one component stretches to all four card lists without flag parameters
app/src/app/util.ts:4-40 — small focused helpers (humanize, dexNumber, orDash) reused everywhere

abstraction_design.rationale: The card/data abstractions are designed around the app's actual variation and stretch well; the weakness is that detail pages and resolvers share no scaffold, so a similar new section is largely a copy.

findings.issue: The not-found recipe (catch → setTitle('Not found – Pokédex') → RESPONSE_INIT.status = 404) is duplicated in five files (pokemon/move/ability/type resolvers and not-found-view).
findings.suggestion: Extract a `markNotFound(title: Title)` helper (or a route-level error/redirect strategy) so 404 semantics change in one place.

findings.issue: CardEntry construction exists in two places (home.ts pageEntries and PokedexData.cardsFor), so adding a card field or fixing card data means editing both, and they can drift.
findings.suggestion: Move species→CardEntry mapping into PokedexData (e.g. `cardsForSpecies(list)`) and let home consume it.

findings.issue: Document titles are set ad-hoc in 11 places across 8 files (each resolver's success and failure paths, home, type-list, not-found-view), scattering the `<h1> – Pokédex` convention.
findings.suggestion: Centralize title formatting in one helper (e.g. `pageTitle(heading)`) called from each site, or use the router's TitleStrategy.

findings.issue: Caching policy is split across three layers (Api promise cache, PokedexData memoized datasets, HttpClient transfer cache in app.config.ts:11), and the root-scoped Api cache never evicts successful entries on a long-lived SSR server.
findings.suggestion: Consolidate cache policy in Api (TTL/size bound), keep PokedexData as a thin client of it, and document the layering.

findings.issue: The default API base `http://localhost:9000` is duplicated in api.ts and server.ts:16, and the config.js contract spans index.html:9, server.ts and api.ts.
findings.suggestion: Define the default once (shared module) and keep the three touching files to just the seam, not the value.

findings.issue: The type-label mapping `typeNames.get(name) ?? humanize(name)` is re-inlined in four places across three resolvers.
findings.suggestion: Expose `typeLabel(ref)` on PokedexData next to typeNames().

findings.issue: The component renders the raw API `EvolutionNode` model directly, so API shape changes ripple into the view layer.
findings.suggestion: Map the chain to a small view model (species name + label) in pokemon.resolver.ts, like every other section on the page.

findings.issue: All styles are global; feature styles (cards, moves tables, filters) are not colocated with their components, so removing or restyling a feature means editing the shared stylesheet and trusting class-name conventions.
findings.suggestion: Move feature-specific blocks into component styles, keeping only tokens and the shell in styles.css.

findings.issue: app.ts points at an empty app.css (dead file), and the project has zero unit specs despite vitest and an `ng test` script being wired up.
findings.suggestion: Delete the empty file and add specs for the highest-leverage pure logic (cardsFor, sorting, filters) to guard future edits.

summary: A cleanly layered Angular 22 app: per-route component/resolver pairs, narrow per-page view models, and a CardEntry/PokedexData abstraction that gives the hardest cross-cutting problems (ref→species mapping, sprite URLs, card rendering) a single home, so most bug fixes land in one place. The recurring editability tax is copy-pasted resolver boilerplate — 404 handling in five files, title formatting in eleven call sites — plus a second card-construction site in the home page and caching rules spread over three layers. Extending with a similar resource page means copying an existing resolver/component pair rather than reusing a scaffold.
